text.title: Hipaa Phi Data Flow Design Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete data-flow design for a clinician portal with five hops (API, PostgreSQL, snapshots, Sentry under a BAA, and a de-identified embeddings API), with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad design (full clinical notes to an embeddings vendor with no BAA, plaintext inside the VPC, a shared ops login) showing what the validator and the reviewer reject.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: careportal-api serves clinician encounter views and appointment scheduling. Patient charts live in PostgreSQL on RDS with nightly snapshots to S3. Errors go to Sentry. Product wants semantic search over clinical notes through a hosted embeddings API. The organisation's Security Officer must sign the design before the search feature ships.

backup restore replays tombstones (runbooks/deletion.md); Sentry per-event deletion API by mrn"} ], "media_disposal_procedure": "runbooks/media-disposal.md: NIST SP 800-88 purge for any drive or device that held PHI; cloud volumes are KMS-encrypted and keys are destroyed on decommission", "review": {"status": "ready_for_review", "security_officer": "security-officer@careportal.example", "approved_by_agent": false} }
example.note: The snapshot bucket and Sentry are hops in their own right, each with identifier classes, encryption, access and retention: the two places a design most often forgets to draw (r-phi-every-hop-inventoried).

The embeddings hop carries an empty `identifier_classes` list because the note text is Safe Harbor de-identified before the call; that is why it needs no BAA even though it is external. Had product insisted on identified notes, the hop would need a BAA for that vendor's specific plan plus a documented identified use (r-phi-minimum-necessary-per-hop, r-phi-baa-for-every-external-hop).

Sentry receives one identifier class (the MRN in the request path) under a BAA that names the plan and the covered service, not just the vendor; the body and headers never reach it because the allow-list scrubber runs first (r-phi-baa-for-every-external-hop, r-phi-never-in-logs-errors-or-urls).

Every link records where TLS terminates: the API-to-RDS link terminates at the RDS endpoint with `rds.force_ssl=1`, not at a load balancer, so there is no plaintext hop inside the VPC (r-phi-encrypted-in-transit-and-at-rest).

The audit store is CloudWatch with a retention lock at 7 years (above the 6-year floor), carries record ids and never field values, and the bulk-access alarm fires at 200 distinct records in 10 minutes by one identity (r-phi-audit-event-per-access).

The deletion path names the two copies a chart can reach (snapshots and Sentry events) and the mechanism for each; the embeddings vendor is not listed because its zero-retention endpoint keeps nothing (r-phi-retention-and-deletion-per-store).
`review.status` is `ready_for_review` with the Security Officer named; signing and `signed_on` are theirs. The agent's flag is the last thing it does (human checkpoint, 45 CFR §164.308(a)(2)).

example.note: Validator output (abridged to the subject findings): `$.hops[0].access.shared_accounts: must equal False, got True`, `$.hops[0].access.auto_logoff_minutes: 0 violates minimum=1`, `$.hops[1].encryption_at_rest: missing required field`, `$.hops[2].baa: missing required field`, `$.hops[2].identified_use_documented_at: missing required field`, `$.links[0].tls_version: '1.0' not in enum ['1.2', '1.3']`, `$.audit_log.append_only: must equal True, got False`, `$.audit_log.contains_phi_field_values: must equal False, got True`, `$.audit_log.retention_years: 1 violates minimum=6`, `$.audit_log.event_fields: no item matches 'contains' {'const': 'identity'}` (and record_id, originating_system), `$.log_scrubbing.phi_in_urls_or_query_strings: must equal False, got True`, `$.log_scrubbing.synthetic_record_test.covers_every_request_path: must equal True, got False`, `$.log_scrubbing.synthetic_record_test.runs_in_ci: must equal True, got False`, `$.deletion_propagation: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.media_disposal_procedure: length 3 below minLength=5`, `$.review.approved_by_agent: must equal False, got True`, `$.review.security_officer: missing required field`, `$.review.signed_on: missing required field`.

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: no hop for the snapshots or the error tracker although both exist in the account (r-phi-every-hop-inventoried); `patient.*` with the justification "simpler than selecting columns" is the opposite of minimum necessary (r-phi-minimum-necessary-per-hop); full clinical notes with names, MRNs and dates going to an embeddings vendor with no BAA is a disclosure the organisation would have to notify (r-phi-baa-for-every-external-hop).
